Kevin Trudeau bought Bitcoin at a dollar. He still brings up the part he got wrong.

A friend told him to buy it at 50 cents first. He didn't listen - and he calls that blown opportunity the real lesson, not the win that came after.

What changed things afterward: he decided to always listen to people who already have what he wants and have already been where he's trying to go. He calls it having a high 'teachability index' - a willingness to learn, a willingness to change.

Most people in their 20s think they already know it all. He did too, once.

#kevintrudeau #bitcoin #mindset #investing #wealthmindset #successmindset

Kevin Trudeau says he laughed at every stock he was ever told to buy.

Apple? 'What a stupid name for a computer company, it's a piece of fruit.' Amazon? 'Books online - that's insane, people want to hold the product.' DirectTV? '500 channels, who even watches that much TV?'

He bought all three anyway, plus Bitcoin at a dollar, because of one rule: listen to people who already have what you want and have already been where you are.

Seeing the potential mattered more than being right about the joke.

What's the 'stupid' idea you're dismissing right now?

#kevintrudeau #investing #wealthmindset #mindset #stockmarket #success

Kevin Trudeau is banned from blackjack in casinos worldwide. He's in something called the Griffin book - a list of players who never cheat, but count too well to let play.

So he switched games. He built his own algorithm for Baccarat, a game everyone said was pure coin-flip luck, and won his daily target 100% of the time for eighteen straight months.

Then Steve Wynn called. Not to ban him - to pay him a fortune to teach the system to Wynn's own gamblers.

Kevin asked why. Wynn's answer: because they'll get overconfident, stop following it, and lose it all back anyway.

A system only works if you actually stick to it.

#kevintrudeau #casino #baccarat #mindset #discipline #wealthmindset

Three professional traders. Three completely different systems. Same 15 seconds.

Kevin Trudeau asked them to just tell him what to do, trading-wise. They told him he wouldn't actually follow it, so they proved the point instead: on the next Fed rate decision, each one called their trade out loud right before executing it.

One went long. One went short. The third didn't decide until ten seconds before. All three made six figures, in the same 15 seconds, doing the opposite of each other.

The method mattered less than actually having the conviction to execute it.

Which one would you have trusted?

#kevintrudeau #trading #investing #mindset #wealthmindset #discipline

Kevin Trudeau once partnered with the second richest man in Australia - the biggest yacht in Sydney Harbour, 60 luxury cars, all paid in cash.

The man made his fortune trading stocks, and he gave his method away for free: a weekly newsletter. 'I bought this at this price. I sold this at that price.' Nothing fancy - 5%, 10% gains, over and over, never one big home-run bet.

Everyone who just copied the trades made money every single time he did.

The ones who thought they were smarter than him, who started improvising their own picks instead? They faltered.

Would you have had the discipline to just copy the winner?

#kevintrudeau #investing #wealthmindset #stockmarket #mindset #success

Two railroads once tried to extort John D. Rockefeller. They were the only way to move his kerosene, so they tripled the price and figured he had no choice.

He went from a fortune to nearly broke overnight. Then he looked at his own refineries and realized oil moves through pipes. He built the first pipeline across America and cut the railroads out completely. His profits went up 10x.

Years later, the government broke up Standard Oil as a monopoly, trying to cut him down for good. Instead, his stock in the 36 companies they split it into made him five times richer within a year.

Every attack on him became the thing that made him more money.

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #mindset #businesshistory #success #money

A mentor once told Kevin Trudeau: when you walk into any room, walk in like you own it.

Kevin said the obvious thing back - easy when you already have the money. The mentor's answer stuck for life: the money doesn't give you the attitude, the attitude gives you the money. When you're broke, just say you're a little illiquid at the moment.

Years later he watched a TV character use that exact line after losing everything, standing in front of a $30 million painting.

A man on one of his cruises waited two full years for a Rolex he couldn't afford, then paid cash the day it finally arrived.

Dream big before the money shows up.

Kevin Trudeau walked into a casino and turned it into a 45% return in four days.

His rule, before he ever sat down: a win goal (the number he's leaving with), a loss limit (the number that makes him walk away), and a time limit. He hit one of the first two almost every single time - some days in six minutes.

Meanwhile, he says most people in that casino walk out with nothing. Not because the game beat them. Because they never set a number to walk away at - winning or losing, they just keep playing until the money runs out.

The same rule works in the market. Do you have a number, or are you just hoping?
